sources.locator: PDF p. 10, Section 4.3, individual-level semantic divergence
sources.quote: At individual level, the average semantic divergence from the centroid per participant was M= 0.28 (SD = 0.03) for unaided ideas and M= 0.29 (SD = 0.03) for AI-assisted ideas.

sources.locator: PDF p. 10, Section 4.3, paired-samples t-test

estimates.notes: The printed means imply greater divergence with AI, but the abstract, Results interpretation and Discussion describe lower divergence. The t statistic, d, confidence bounds and arm labels are transcribed exactly; no direction has been repaired from the narrative. The confidence-interval target, subtraction order and d standardizer are not identified. Methods describe within-person pairwise distances; Results describe distances from an unspecified centroid per participant. unit and sd_level retain the explicitly described participant level, and within_person retains the stated paired test. However, t(364) is inconsistent with the reported study of 51 people, so analysis-specific participant counts and se_basis remain null. Null se_basis means the implemented independent units are unresolved, not that the paper omitted a test. No participant count is inferred from degrees of freedom, and no values are digitized from Fig. 3.

estimates.question: across_people
estimates.measure_detail: Cosine distance of each idea description's LaBSE embedding from the mean embedding of its condition. Both tasks are pooled; text was extracted through Gemini OCR and manually verified (PDF p. 7, Section 3.3.2).

sources.locator: PDF p. 10, Section 4.3, group-level semantic divergence
sources.quote: At group level, the average semantic divergence to the centroid was M= 0.28 (SD = 0.06) for unaided ideas and M= 0.29 (SD = 0.07) for AI-assisted ideas.

sources.locator: PDF p. 10, Section 4.3, independent-samples t-test

estimates.notes: The printed means imply greater divergence with AI, whereas the narrative concludes greater similarity. The signed t, d and confidence bounds are retained exactly as printed. The confidence-interval target, subtraction order and d standardizer are not specified. The independent-samples test analyzes idea-to-condition-centroid distances with no reported participant adjustment; se_basis is output and within_person is null. The same students contribute several ideas and appear in both conditions. n_units is null because the semantic-analysis observation count is not explicitly reported. The separately reported corpus total is 728 ideas (PDF p. 5, Section 3.2.1: "In total, 728 ideas were gathered."); this is descriptive context only, not a confirmed semantic-analysis sample size. The printed t(728) is inconsistent with a conventional independent-samples test on that corpus; the actual semantic-analysis sample and analysis-specific participant counts remain unresolved. Both tasks are pooled. No numbers are digitized from Fig. 3.

The participant-level paired description conflicts with t(364) in a study of 51 people. The actual independent-unit basis is unknown; se_basis and analysis-specific participant counts are null (PDF pp. 4, 7, 10).

The implemented semantic-analysis sample and degrees of freedom need clarification; n_units is null because the corpus total is not a confirmed analysis count. This is explicitly an output-level test without reported participant adjustment (PDF pp. 5, 7, 10).
